question: Sequential use of vacuum extraction followed by forceps delivery (or vice versa) is acceptable clinical practice when the first instrument fails to achieve delivery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Sequential instrumental delivery carries a substantially elevated risk of serious neonatal morbidity. International guidelines recommend abandoning the attempt and proceeding to caesarean section if the first instrument fails, rather than switching instruments.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Sequential instrumental delivery is associated with a significantly increased risk of serious neonatal injury (intracranial haemorrhage, subgaleal haematoma, facial nerve palsy). When one instrument fails, the recommended next step is usually caesarean section, not switching to the alternative instrument.
